items.title: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type (PolyShell)
items.summary: This vulnerability, named 'PolyShell' by Sansec, is an unrestricted file upload flaw that could lead to arbitrary code execution. It was fixed in APSB26-73 and added to the CISA KEV catalog on October 27, 2026, indicating active exploitation.

items.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in Adobe Commerce, including Template Engine Injection (BlockStrap)
items.summary: This bulletin addresses eleven vulnerabilities, with the most critical being CVE-2026-103849 (BlockStrap), a template engine injection with a CVSS score of 10.0 allowing unauthenticated arbitrary code execution. It also includes CVE-2026-92909, an incorrect authorization flaw in B2B allowing unauthenticated code execution.

items.title: Arbitrary Code Execution Vulnerability (StyleSmuggler)
items.summary: This emergency update resolves a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-75650 (StyleSmuggler), that could result in unauthenticated arbitrary code execution and was actively exploited in the wild.

items.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source
items.summary: This security update resolves critical, important, and moderate vulnerabilities, including six exploitable without authentication, that could lead to security feature bypass and privilege escalation.

items.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source, including Incorrect Authorization
items.summary: This update addresses critical, important, and moderate vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-71362, an unauthenticated incorrect authorization flaw (CVSS 9.1) that could result in privilege escalation.

items.title: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution and Customer Account Takeover
items.summary: Discovered in August 2025, this critical flaw (CVSS 9.1) allows customer account takeover and unauthenticated remote code execution under certain conditions, with mass attacks observed starting October 22, 2026.

items.title: Incorrect Authorization in Adobe Commerce B2B
items.summary: Part of APSB26-153, this vulnerability affects Adobe Commerce B2B and allows unauthenticated code execution with a CVSS score of 9.8.

items.title: Stored Cross-site Scripting (XSS) with Privilege Escalation
items.summary: Addressed in APSB26-153, this is a critical stored XSS vulnerability that can be associated with privilege escalation.

items.title: Stored Cross-site Scripting (XSS) with Privilege Escalation
items.summary: Included in APSB26-153, this is another critical stored XSS vulnerability that can lead to privilege escalation.

items.title: Stored Cross-site Scripting (XSS)
items.summary: This high-severity stored XSS vulnerability is part of the APSB26-153 update.

items.title: Stored Cross-site Scripting (XSS)
items.summary: Another high-severity stored XSS vulnerability addressed in the APSB26-153 security bulletin.

items.title: Incorrect Authorization in Adobe Commerce B2B
items.summary: This high-severity incorrect authorization vulnerability in Adobe Commerce B2B can result in security feature bypasses, as detailed in APSB26-153.

items.title: Incorrect Authorization in Adobe Commerce B2B
items.summary: Another high-severity incorrect authorization flaw in Adobe Commerce B2B that can lead to security feature bypasses, fixed in APSB26-153.
